Add yet another spinlock for the TDP MMU and take it when marking indirect
shadow pages unsync.  When using the TDP MMU and L1 is running L2(s) with
nested TDP
column2: KVM may encounter shadow pages for the TDP entries managed by

column1: L1 (controlling L2) when handling a TDP MMU page fault.  The unsync logic
is not thread safe
column2: e.g. the kvm_mmu_page fields are not atomic

column1: misbehaves when a shadow page is marked unsync via a TDP MMU page fault
which runs with mmu_lock held for read
Lack of a critical section manifests most visibly as an underflow of
unsync_children in clear_unsync_child_bit() due to unsync_children being
corrupted when multiple CPUs write it without a critical section and
without atomic operations.  But underflow is the best case scenario.  The
worst case scenario is that unsync_children prematurely hits '0' and
leads to guest memory corruption due to KVM neglecting to properly sync
shadow pages.
Use an entirely new spinlock even though piggybacking tdp_mmu_pages_lock
would functionally be ok.  Usurping the lock could degrade performance when
building upper level page tables on different vCPUs
unsync flow could hold the lock for a comparatively long time depending on
the number of indirect shadow pages and the depth of the paging tree.
For simplicity
column2: take the lock for all MMUs

column1: easily know that mmu_lock is held for write.  If mmu_lock is held for
write
column2: there cannot be contention for the inner spinlock

column1: shadow pages unsync across multiple vCPUs will be slow enough that
bouncing the kvm_arch cacheline should be in the noise.
Note
column2: even though L2 could theoretically be given access to its own EPT

column1: entries
column2: a nested MMU must hold mmu_lock for write and thus cannot race

column1: against a TDP MMU page fault.  I.e. the additional spinlock only _needs_ to
be taken by the TDP MMU
column2: as opposed to being taken by any MMU for a VM

column1: that is running with the TDP MMU enabled.  Holding mmu_lock for read also
prevents the indirect shadow page from being freed.  But as above
it simple and always take the lock.
Alternative #1
column2: the TDP MMU could simply pass ""false"" for can_unsync and

column1: effectively disable unsync behavior for nested TDP.  Write protecting leaf
shadow pages is unlikely to noticeably impact traditional L1 VMMs
VMMs typically don't modify TDP entries
column2: but the same may not hold true for

column1: non-standard use cases and/or VMMs that are migrating physical pages (from
L1's perspective).
Alternative #2
column2: the unsync logic could be made thread safe.  In theory

column1: simply converting all relevant kvm_mmu_page fields to atomics and using
atomic bitops for the bitmap would suffice.  However
would be required
column2: (b) the code churn would be substantial

column1: shadow paging would incur additional atomic operations in performance
sensitive paths for no benefit (to legacy shadow paging).
